An object moving along a curve in the $x y$-plane is at position $(x(t), y(t))$ at time $t$, where
$$
\frac{d x}{d t}=\tan \left(e^{-t}\right) \text { and } \frac{d y}{d t}=\sec \left(e^{-t}\right)
$$

for $t \geq 0$. At time $t=1$, the object is at position $(2,-3)$.\\
(a) Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve at position $(2,-3)$.\\
(b) Find the acceleration vector and the speed of the object at time $t=1$.\\
(c) Find the total distance traveled by the object over the time interval $1 \leq t \leq 2$.\\
(d) Is there a time $t \geq 0$ at which the object is on the $y$-axis? Explain why or why not.

\section*{Question 2}

An object moving along a curve in the \(x y\)-plane is at position \((x(t), y(t))\) at time \(t\), where
\[
\frac{d x}{d t}=\tan \left(e^{-t}\right) \text { and } \frac{d y}{d t}=\sec \left(e^{-t}\right)
\]
for \(t \geq 0\). At time \(t=1\), the object is at position (2, -3).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve at position \((2,-3)\).
\item[(b)] Find the acceleration vector and the speed of the object at time \(t=1\).
\item[(c)] Find the total distance traveled by the object over the time interval \(1 \leq t \leq 2\).
\item[(d)] Is there a time \(t \geq 0\) at which the object is on the \(y\)-axis? Explain why or why not.
\item[(a)] \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{\frac{d y}{d t}}{\frac{d x}{d t}}=\frac{\sec \left(e^{-t}\right)}{\tan \left(e^{-t}\right)}=\frac{1}{\sin \left(e^{-t}\right)}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{(2,-3)}=\frac{1}{\sin \left(e^{-1}\right)}=2.780 \text { or } 2.781 \\
& y+3=\frac{1}{\sin \left(e^{-1}\right)}(x-2)
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] \(x^{\prime \prime}(1)=-0.42253, y^{\prime \prime}(1)=-0.15196\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& a(1)=\langle-0.423,-0.152\rangle \text { or }\langle-0.422,-0.151\rangle . \\
& \text { speed }=\sqrt{\left(\sec \left(e^{-1}\right)\right)^{2}+\left(\tan \left(e^{-1}\right)\right)^{2}}=1.138 \text { or } 1.139
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] \(\int_{1}^{2} \sqrt{\left(x^{\prime}(t)\right)^{2}+\left(y^{\prime}(t)\right)^{2}} d t=1.059\)
\item[(d)] \(x(0)=x(1)-\int_{0}^{1} x^{\prime}(t) d t=2-0.775553>0\)
The particle starts to the right of the \(y\)-axis.
Since \(x^{\prime}(t)>0\) for all \(t \geq 0\), the object is always moving to the right and thus is never on the \(y\)-axis.
\end{itemize}
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1:\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{(2,-3)} \\ 1: \text { equation of tangent line }\end{array}\right.\)
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { acceleration vector } \\ 1: \text { speed }\end{array}\right.\)
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integral } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: x(0) \text { expression } \\ 1: x^{\prime}(t)>0 \\ 1: \text { conclusion and reason }\end{array}\right.\)
